evidence.exact_quote: The **Artifacts panel** is the single place to see everything agents produced during a run or thread: file changes (diffs), plans, verification evidence, screenshots, reasoning summaries, browser recordings, tool/LLM traces, cost_usage attribution, and other types below. It does not run agents; it lists, previews, and links. All artifact types listed are **required** for MVP; there are no optional types.

**Option 2 only:** One seglog event type per artifact type. No single generic `runtime_artifact` event with a subtype field. Each persisted event uses the canonical EventRecord envelope in `Plans/Contracts_V0.md#EventRecord`; this document owns the runtime-artifact event taxonomy and payload schema requirements, not the EventRecord field set. The persisted EventRecord `event_type` value is exactly one of the 19 event type names below.

items.impact: This provides a closed producer taxonomy and prevents generic-event drift.
items.statement: The panel is expressly read-only with respect to execution, all listed runtime artifact families are MVP-required, and persistence uses one exact EventRecord event_type per family rather than a generic subtype event.
items.title: Closed 19-family runtime artifact taxonomy

evidence.exact_quote: - Runtime artifact lookup/indexing remains a projection concern rather than canonical artifact truth.

Runtime artifacts that bridge receipts, Usage, Ledger, Debug, and exported evidence use the shared attribution packet from §4B plus the following artifact-panel rules. Owner docs keep their primary schema authority: `Plans/Contracts_V0.md` owns shared event names and temporal primitives; `Plans/storage-plan.md` owns persisted state mechanics, retention storage, and projector behavior; this document owns the runtime-artifact panel contract and artifact-family envelope.

items.impact: The index can fail or rebuild without silently becoming artifact authority.
items.statement: Canonical artifact truth stays in runtime evidence, storage owns projector mechanics, Contracts owns shared wrappers and temporal primitives, and this document owns the artifact-family envelope and panel contract.
items.title: Projection and owner boundaries are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime-artifact route-state answers "where should the user land," not "how should every panel be laid out when they get there." Artifact, receipt, usage, and export pivots resolve canonical IDs/refs and object identity first: `artifact_id`, `run_id`, `thread_id`, `node_id?`, `attempt_id`, `receipt_id?`, `provider_attempt_ref?`, and `usage_event_ref?`.

Receipt-like exports and manifest-backed bundles preserve canonical run/thread/attempt linkage and must not mint shadow IDs. Usage-linked artifacts continue to route through canonical usage identity rather than artifact-local usage models.

items.impact: Consumers can deep-link without making tab or docking state part of object identity.
items.statement: Cross-surface pivots resolve canonical object identity before destination layout, and exports preserve the same run, thread, attempt, usage, and receipt lineage.
items.title: Object route-state precedes shell-state

evidence.exact_quote: `usage_event_ref` is a locator-grade usage bridge on runtime artifacts. It is stable for the lifetime of the referenced Usage/Ledger record, scoped to the canonical project/run or account-backed usage record, and present whenever the artifact is cost-bearing or can pivot to Usage/Ledger history. Runtime artifacts MUST NOT use `usage_event_ref` as a replacement `artifact_id`, `attempt_id`, or route primary key.

- `cost_usage` artifacts MUST carry `usage_event_ref` whenever available (`usage_event_ref?` in older optional notation). When traceable, they also carry `attempt_id`, `node_id`, and `provider_attempt_ref` so Usage, Ledger, Run Graph, and the Artifacts panel can explain who produced the artifact and why it exists in the execution graph.

**Per-type:** One file per artifact type, e.g. Plans/runtime_artifact_code_diff.schema.json through Plans/runtime_artifact_artifact_version.schema.json, with `$id`: pm.runtime_artifact.<type>.v1. Each payload is validated against the envelope plus the corresponding type schema. The cost_usage schema MUST include required `usage_event_ref`, normalized provider/usage/cost/quota/authority/refs/flags objects, and required `reasoning_tokens` (integer, minimum 0) as the schema wire alias for UF-085 `reasoning/thoughts`, backed by `counting_semantics` and no-double-count rules. The tool_llm_trace schema MUST include required `trace_ref`, trace lifecycle, provider-attempt, usage-settlement, retry/escalation, and raw-payload/redaction refs. The api_web_call and browser_recording schemas MUST reject arbitrary non-empty payloads and enforce their web operation / browser session discriminators. All 19 type schemas are required; no optional schema files.

items.impact: A cost-bearing artifact can be either rejected, persisted without its promised join, or blocked indefinitely while waiting for a Usage record.
items.statement: The locator is mandatory for cost-bearing artifacts, conditionally mandatory whenever available in another rule, and schema-required without a defined no-reference state. Provider outages or delayed Usage projection therefore have no valid artifact state.
items.title: cost_usage usage_event_ref cardinality is contradictory

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime artifacts declare an explicit retention class:
- `ephemeral_view` for active UI frames, transient stream chunks, and non-canonical preview state that may be discarded after the owning view no longer needs it.

items.impact: Durable evidence can be deleted too early, ephemeral sensitive data can persist, and recovery behavior can vary by implementation.
items.statement: Three retention classes are named, but the excerpt does not define assignment authority, TTL calculation, legal or evidence holds, promotion and demotion, export interaction, deletion receipts, failed deletion, or concurrent reader behavior.
items.title: Retention classes lack lifecycle transitions and deletion authority

evidence.exact_quote: Streaming and incremental runtime artifacts preserve `truncation_state`, flushed-sequence or equivalent committed-offset metadata, and explicit gap-rendering rules so viewers can distinguish complete evidence, intentionally omitted ranges, dropped stream chunks, and unknown continuity. Diff, review, and export artifacts MUST state the `raw-content-vs-metadata` boundary before storing or exporting changed-line bodies, comments, screenshots, traces, or logs.

Persisted stream-view intent is explicit. Stream surfaces distinguish `follow`, `paused_snapshot`, and `historical_view`; after restart, `follow` may resume only after source revalidation, while `paused_snapshot` and `historical_view` reopen as bounded historical evidence with visible degradation when the live source cannot be recovered.

items.impact: Two viewers can present the same partial evidence as complete, duplicate chunks after restart, or resume from different offsets.
items.statement: The stream modes and visible gap requirement are useful, but source revalidation, committed-offset comparison, resume versus fork behavior, irrecoverable-gap closure, and offline transition rules are not defined.
items.title: Stream restart and gap recovery have no decision oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Temporary instrumentation artifacts declare `instrumentation_id`, `collector_state` (`collector-state` in audit vocabulary), install/collect/remove lifecycle state, evidence sink, cleanup or rollback state, and owning Debug investigation refs. Debug instrumentation MUST NOT outlive its declared cleanup policy without an explicit failed-cleanup artifact or blocked recovery record.

items.impact: Collectors can survive closed investigations, duplicate cleanup can remove active instrumentation, and support cannot tell whether retry is safe.
items.statement: A failed-cleanup artifact is required, but no cleanup authority, idempotency key, lease, timeout, retry ceiling, collector crash race, investigation-close ordering, or rollback outcome contract is supplied.
items.title: Instrumentation cleanup is observable but not race-safe

evidence.exact_quote: - importing a bundle creates an `imported_bundle` debug target and preserves provenance about the external source rather than pretending the bundle is a live local runtime target
- redacted, revoked, blocked, expired, and omitted items remain visible in the manifest summary so users can tell what was or was not carried forward

items.impact: A crafted external bundle can inject unsafe paths or links, exhaust resources, spoof evidence, or expose unredacted material.
items.statement: Import preserves provenance and creates an imported target, but the excerpt does not require schema validation, content hashes or signatures, archive/path traversal defense, URI allowlisting, size limits, quarantine, malware handling, or fail-closed rendering.
items.title: Imported investigation bundles lack an untrusted-input boundary

evidence.exact_quote: Sensitive and operational metadata minimization applies before export defaults are chosen. Secret material is redacted by policy, and non-secret operational metadata is still masked or omitted when it can expose account, host, path, provider, or workspace context outside the selected export profile.

items.impact: Different export paths can leak account, host, path, provider, workspace, or protected project context despite a nominal redaction profile.
items.statement: The plan requires masking or omission but does not identify who selects the export profile, how nested and binary artifacts are scanned, whether redaction failure blocks export, how overrides are authorized, or how disclosure is audited.
items.title: Export minimization lacks policy selection and failure semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Runtime Artifacts must be able to project provider-native artifact envelopes for generated media, provider receipts, streamed logs/events, model catalogs, route/probe evidence, support-state transitions, adoption/drift/blocked states, and repair/retry records. Artifacts reference provider_entry_id, account_profile_ref, model_id, media_route_id, requested/effective identity, source_confidence, verification_state, redaction_profile, and permission_snapshot_id while excluding secret material. Antigravity projections must distinguish public `agy` model catalog artifacts from the separate OAuth/internal `gemini-3.1-flash-image` generated-media route proof.
- Do not flatten partial-success or gated provider states into generic failure.

items.impact: Provider artifacts remain inspectable without collapsing trust states or persisting credentials.
items.statement: RAP-032 requires account, model, route, confidence, verification, redaction, and permission references while distinguishing public catalog evidence from private generated-media route proof.
items.title: Provider-native projections preserve route identity and exclude secrets

evidence.exact_quote: Generated media artifacts must project provider receipt metadata, generation parameters, provider/base response status, trace/request id where available, hashes, durable local artifact refs, original provider URL refs, expiry warnings, partial success/failure counts, and provenance caveats. MiniMax Image-01 URL outputs require 24-hour expiry disclosure; OpenAI/Codex Images 2 routes require account/route distinction and C2PA/SynthID caveats; subscription-backed routes require support-state and terms-risk refs. Antigravity OAuth/internal `gemini-3.1-flash-image` receipts require private/unofficial endpoint caveats, non-secret request/proof refs, image dimensions/hash, and support-state labels.

items.impact: Users can distinguish durable captures from expiring provider locations and caveated provenance from trust guarantees.
items.statement: RAP-033 preserves provider status, request and trace metadata, hashes, durable local references, expiring original URLs, partial counts, and route-specific provenance caveats without storing secrets.
items.title: Generated-media receipts expose expiry, partial outcomes, and provenance caveats

evidence.exact_quote: - URL expiry and durable artifact capture status are visible.
- Partial successes are represented with counts and failed-item metadata where available.

items.impact: Provider URLs can expire before capture, retries can duplicate successful items, and a partial batch cannot be deterministically resumed.
items.statement: Expiry and durable-capture status are visible, but no deadline scheduling, proactive capture, refresh eligibility, retry relation, cancellation, duplicate suppression, failed-item identity, or rollback state is required.
items.title: Expiring and partially successful media lack recovery transitions

evidence.exact_quote: Evidence and artifact lists use independent virtualization and `/paging`. Heavy artifacts remain `metadata-first` until opened, and artifact previews are demand-loaded rather than `pre-rendered` for long lists. This keeps Evidence exact without forcing every artifact body into memory or preview rows before the user asks for it.

The artifact index is a projection for lookup, `/filter/navigation`, and panel recovery, not canonical artifact truth. It must be rebuildable from seglog and the runtime-artifact envelope; missing or `/corrupt` index rows degrade to `record-backed` views rather than implying artifact loss. The storage owner registers the `/index` key family, lifecycle, failure states, and `/rebuild` behavior as a first-class projection family.

items.impact: The panel need not load every body, and projection loss does not imply artifact loss.
items.statement: Independent paging, metadata-first rows, demand-loaded previews, and record-backed degradation are explicit.
items.title: Long lists and index loss have bounded GUI behavior

evidence.exact_quote: Completed browser evidence should survive crash and recovery when possible.

items.impact: Completed evidence can disappear or be shown as complete after a crash with implementation-dependent behavior.
items.statement: The phrase when possible supplies no durability class, flush boundary, recovery oracle, user disclosure, or distinction between browser-runtime loss and artifact-store failure.
items.title: Browser crash survival is explicitly discretionary

evidence.exact_quote: All artifact differentiators identified in the research are MVP and required; no optional differentiators. Triggers, cardinality, error handling, sanitization, and UI edge cases must be specified per type as needed for implementation.

items.impact: Neither a builder nor an auditor can prove that the MVP includes all differentiators or that each type is implementation-ready.
items.statement: The plan makes every research differentiator mandatory but does not enumerate the research set here and delegates triggers, cardinality, errors, sanitization, and UI edge cases per type as needed.
items.title: MVP differentiator scope is circular and non-falsifiable

evidence.exact_quote: `operation_receipt_record` is a projector and receipt-surface record derived from canonical events, not a replacement for them. Its key joins `run_id`, optional `attempt_id`, `action_family`, and `receipt_id`; the envelope remains cross-surface `/receipt` lineage for Ledger, Usage, Orchestrator, and owner panels.
- Bridge fields remain joins rather than replacement primary keys.

- Usage-linked artifacts consume frozen `effective_*` runtime snapshot fields and `source_confidence` fields. The legacy `usage-source-confidence` spelling remains preserved only as compatibility/source-lineage vocabulary; Agent-Config and Health may display live current values beside the artifact, but they must not rename or rewrite the frozen schema carried by the usage/runtime record.

items.impact: Ledger, Usage, Orchestrator, and owner panels can inspect the same historical outcome without current settings mutating it.
items.statement: The derived operation receipt is not event authority, tier_id is compatibility-only, bridge fields remain joins, and live configuration cannot rewrite frozen effective or confidence values.
items.title: Receipt bridge viewer preserves frozen lineage

evidence.exact_quote: The common envelope pins `artifact_id`, `artifact_type`, canonical IDs, `run_id`, `thread_id?`, `node_id?`, `attempt_id`, `provider_attempt_ref?`, `usage_event_ref?`, receipt refs, producer/actor refs, content refs, projection fields, and routing refs. Per-type schemas may add required fields for a specific `runtime_artifact.*` family, but they must not drift from or override those envelope fields.

items.impact: Failed-attempt and subagent artifacts can remain unattributable or use incompatible producer shapes.
items.statement: The envelope promises producer/actor refs but does not pin field names, requiredness, cardinality, actor-versus-process semantics, delegation lineage, anonymous producer behavior, or stability across retry.
items.title: Producer and actor identity fields are named only as abstract refs
